item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 20, 2026
item.description: WTI October settled $99.53 (-2.3%) and Brent November $103.19 (-1.6%) on Friday, while the Canadian diff complex heads into the week with no fresh public prints.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 21, 2026
item.description: Keystone ran at 94% of available capacity, rail's share of exports rose to 7.1% in June, and the WTI October contract expires Tuesday.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 22, 2026
item.description: Yanbu exports could resume today, Brent fell $2+ to its lowest since Sep 8, and the WTI October contract expired after a four-session slide of roughly $10.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 23, 2026
item.description: "Reconstructed edition — the morning run failed; rebuilt from the day's wires and the following edition. WTI and Brent closed Tuesday at two-week lows after six straight down days; the Saudi East-West restart was confirmed; EIA weekly due Wednesday morning."

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 24, 2026
item.description: "Flat price rallied 3–4% Wednesday on a diesel-export-ban headline the White House then denied, plus fresh Hormuz attacks. The EIA's bearish 3-million-barrel build was shrugged off. Joliet still dark; diesel cracks over $100 keep synthetic crude bid."

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 25, 2026
item.description: "Brent and WTI giving back Thursday's Houthi-missile rally on overnight US–Iran truce signals. Several Joliet units returned Wednesday — the front-of-strip WCS catalyst. Diesel cracks re-testing records; October Merey sales stalled on record freight."
